The Toboso were an Indigenous people of the Bolsón de Mapimí, a desert basin in what is now eastern Chihuahua and western Coahuila, northern Mexico. They were linked to the Jumano and to the people of La Junta de los Ríos on the Rio Grande, and lived mainly by hunting and gathering.

Their land lay close to the Spanish mining frontier of New Spain, and slave raids for mine labour drove them to fight. From the mid 1600s they raided Spanish ranches, settlements and mule trains, and Spanish soldiers waged long campaigns against them. By the early 1700s war, enslavement and disease had broken them, and survivors merged into other groups, including the Apache who moved into the Bolsón. Their western neighbours were the Concho.
